paragraphs: Rabbi Yehudah ben Lakish. (A tanna of a baraita.)

In [Kohelet Rabbah 1:15](https://www.sefaria.org/Kohelet_Rabbah.1.15.2) we find Yehudah ben Lakish teaching in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Gamliel. In the Sifra, Acharei, at the printed locator קלא, the attribution is given as “רש״בג in the name of רש״בל.” Hyman regards this as an error: he proposes that it should read “Rabbi Yehudah ben Lakish says in the name of רש״בג,” citing Yalkut Joshua, remez 23, in support.[^1]

He is also mentioned in baraitot: [Shabbat 43b](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.43b.8); [Yoma 53b](https://www.sefaria.org/Yoma.53b.16) and [85a](https://www.sefaria.org/Yoma.85a.8); [Chagigah 9b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chagigah.9b.16); and in [Yerushalmi Sanhedrin, chapter 1, halakhah 1](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Sanhedrin.1.1.27); [Mekhilta, Yitro, Parashat BaChodesh, chapter 1](https://www.sefaria.org/Mekhilta_DeRabbi_Yishmael%2C_Tractate_Bachodesh.1.15); and [Tosefta Sotah, chapter 7](https://www.sefaria.org/Tosefta_Sotah.7.9).[^2]

notes.text: The corresponding digital [Sifra, Acharei Mot 8:7](https://www.sefaria.org/Sifra%2C_Acharei_Mot%2C_Section_8.7) reads “Shimon ben Gamliel in the name of Shimon ben Lakish.” [Yalkut Shimoni on Nach 23:6](https://www.sefaria.org/Yalkut_Shimoni_on_Nach.23.6) instead has “Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel in the name of Yehudah ben Lakish.” Both run in the opposite direction to Hyman’s proposed replacement; the second name also differs. The Kohelet passage titles Shimon ben Gamliel Rabbi, while the Yalkut calls him Rabban.

Hyman leaves the sides of Shabbat 43, Yoma 85 and Chagigah 9 unspecified. The linked occurrences name Yehudah ben Lakish directly. Yoma 53b puts בן לקיש in parentheses. See [Heilprin’s entry](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=1660&lang=en) for a comparison of several of these locators.
